text: When choosing between eigenmode expansion (EME) and the beam propagation method (BPM), which statement correctly distinguishes them?
choices: BPM is bidirectional and captures reflections; EME is one-way
EME cost grows with device length; BPM cost is length-independent
EME is bidirectional (captures reflections) and its cost is set by mode/section count rather than length; BPM makes a one-way paraxial approximation and cannot model reflections or resonators
Both fail at low index contrast and are used only for high-contrast sharp bends
explanation: EME cascades scattering matrices bidirectionally, so a uniform region is a free phase matrix (cost independent of length), while BPM marches a one-way paraxial envelope and cannot handle reflections, resonators, high index contrast, or sharp bends. Choice 0 swaps the two; choice 1 is backwards (EME cost is length-independent); choice 3 inverts BPM's regime, which is long, low-contrast, reflection-free structures.
